refactor(text): drop the legacy overflow option from truncate (rich-subtraction-8wh.3, .4)

RichText.truncate accepted `{ mode, marker }` and a legacy
`{ overflow: "fold" | "crop" | "ellipsis" }`, and derived the marker
through a three-level nested ternary over both. No caller in src/ or
examples/ used the legacy form; one test did.

The option is gone and the marker is `options?.marker ?? "…"`.

Behaviour change: a bare `truncate(width)` used to crop with no
marker, because the ternary only defaulted to "…" when `mode` was
passed. The doc comment already said the default was "…"; the code now
agrees with it. `marker: ""` still crops raw.

The legacy test is rewritten to pin that default (`truncate(6)` on
"hello world" is "hello…"). It lands with .3 rather than as .4 on its
own: `tsconfig.test.json` type-checks test/, so removing the option
turns the old call into an excess-property error and `npm run lint`
fails until the test changes too. No docs page mentions truncate.

docs(readme): one checked demo table for package users (rich-subtraction-8wh.2) (#135)

* docs(readme): one checked demo table for package users (rich-subtraction-8wh.2)

The Demos section had three "Features exercised" tables mapping modules to
how each demo used them, a paragraph on the coverage gate, and an instruction
to run jq against package.json to find the script list. All of it was written
for maintainers. The tables were hand-copied answers to a question
test/coverage/ already computes, and CLAUDE.md already explains the coverage
gate to contributors.

The section now serves someone who has installed the package: the live
gallery first, then how to clone and run a demo, then one table giving each
demo's npm script and a line on what it shows. The per-demo key-binding list
is gone as well, because the interactive demos show their bindings on screen.

test/docs/readme-demos.test.ts holds that table to package.json: the rows must
name exactly the scripts that run dist-demo/examples/<demo>/index.js, each
paired with the demo it runs. Renaming a script or adding a demo now fails
the suite. The test can't check whether a description is still accurate.

docs/demos/index.md said the README lists "what each one exercises"; it now
says what the README actually gives.

* test(docs): count demo scripts that pass arguments (rich-subtraction-8wh.2)
